cases.title: Bing sitelinks: revenue gain with an initial guardrail failure
cases.event_period: Experiment dates not established; report published August 8, 2013.
cases.reported_context: Bing evaluated advertiser sitelinks against revenue and user engagement.
cases.reported_intervention: The first design added sitelinks; a revised design reduced occupied space by lowering average ad count.
cases.reported_outcome: The initial design increased revenue but harmed user metrics. The revision retained revenue benefit with neutral user impact, according to Bing.
limitations: Company-authored retrospective, not independently reanalyzed.
Raw data, uncertainty intervals, exact sample and complete guardrail definitions unavailable here.
Search-ad geometry and population do not establish results for a small SaaS landing page.
cases.original_climbos_application: Require a commercial outcome plus customer-experience guardrails. If one fails, preserve the mechanism hypothesis, inspect the cause, and test a revised design rather than shipping from revenue alone.

cases.title: Power Automate: easier entry did not establish downstream success
cases.event_period: Experiment dates not established; report published September 5, 2023.
cases.reported_context: Microsoft studied discovery of Copilot-assisted flow creation.
cases.reported_intervention: A homepage entry route made access to the experience easier.
cases.reported_outcome: Entry increased, but downstream save behavior was worse in the treatment; the report cautions against declaring success from entry alone.
limitations: Actual data are redacted and funnel description is historical.
Conditional funnel rates require care; the report is not a complete reusable dataset.
Saving is itself a proxy, not proof of realized workflow value or revenue.
cases.original_climbos_application: Track the same eligible cohort through recommendation acceptance, completed setup, executed task, and useful outcome. Do not optimize ClimbOS for owners clicking Generate or approving drafts while execution quality falls.

cases.title: Buffer native versus third-party posting: a reported null difference
cases.event_period: Reported test ran November 27 to December 19, 2017.
cases.reported_context: Buffer compared posting methods across social profiles.
cases.reported_intervention: Participating brands posted through native interfaces and third-party tools, trying to maintain content quality and timing.
cases.reported_outcome: Buffer reported no significant reach or engagement difference in this study.
limitations: Vendor has a commercial interest in third-party publishing.
Content was not identical; schedule execution had misses.
Small per-platform samples and no equivalence margin established here.
Historical results do not certify October 2026 algorithms or every tool.
cases.original_climbos_application: Treat publishing-method penalties as a testable hypothesis. Verify current technical eligibility separately, then compare suitable content and business outcomes; do not encode a universal platform penalty or universal equivalence.

cases.title: Buffer content refresh month: an informative observational trade-off
cases.reported_context: Buffer questioned the need for constant new blog content.
cases.reported_intervention: For a month it focused on repurposing and refreshing existing material rather than fully new articles.
cases.reported_outcome: The report describes a modest total traffic decline, increased organic traffic, and lower social/referral traffic versus the previous month.
limitations: No randomized counterfactual.
Multiple interventions and possible seasonality.
Existing content inventory was a major starting asset.
Traffic changes do not establish incremental customers, contribution, or saved labor.
cases.original_climbos_application: Compare create, update, redistribute, and retire options for existing assets. Require inventory and workload evidence, channel-specific effects, and downstream outcomes before treating reduced publishing as a repeatable strategy.

cases.title: Buffer transparent feedback: an operating practice was reversed
cases.event_period: Early-2015 practice described in an August 17, 2015 retrospective.
cases.reported_context: Buffer extended its transparency principle to constructive employee feedback.
cases.reported_intervention: It tried public constructive feedback and later returned to private feedback while keeping praise public.
cases.reported_outcome: The author reported low participation, enlarged public discussions, and defensiveness; the practice was ended.
limitations: A participant narrative without a controlled comparison.
No quantified productivity or commercial effect established.
Not evidence that transparency fails in general.
Employee-feedback setting differs from customer research.
cases.original_climbos_application: Design correction channels around psychological and practical access. Offer private owner correction and permissioned research channels; do not assume every observation should be shared across a tenant or across customers.

cases.title: Etsy interleaving: validate a faster measurement method before trusting it
cases.event_period: Engineering report published August 8, 2022; experiment dates not established.
cases.reported_context: Etsy sought faster comparisons of search-ranking algorithms.
cases.reported_intervention: It built interleaving, then validated with identical-ranker tests and an A/B wrapper checking performance.
cases.reported_outcome: Etsy reported neutral identical-ranker outcomes and no negative performance impact in initial validation.
limitations: Method is suited to ordered result sets, not arbitrary interface changes.
Preference measurement does not replace every business-outcome experiment.
Published speed improvements are not adopted as ClimbOS forecasts.
Engineering report, not an independently replicated study.
cases.original_climbos_application: Before trusting a new retrieval ranking or evaluator, test identical alternatives, bias, and latency. Use paired ranking comparisons only for eligible ranking tasks, and retain separate end-to-end business-quality evaluation.
